subject: ACME feature-parity: post-call recap & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>, Tom Brooks <tbrooks@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: ACME feature-parity: post-call recap & next tests

Hi Alice / Tom —

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our call and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned:

- Goal: Validate Redwood parity vs your current hyperscaler setup for the three critical flows you highlighted: 1) function/tool calling, 2) structured JSON outputs for downstream ingestion, 3) streaming latencies for incremental UI updates.
- Why this matters: you care about predictable latency under load, exactness of structured outputs (schema adherence), and ability to integrate tool calls in a deterministic way (webhook / binary tool integration).

Proposed next tests (we outlined on the call):
1) Function/tool calling: run a set of 200 concurrent conversations that exercise tool calls (external API invocation pattern + tool error handling). Measure success rate, cold vs warm KV cache behavior, and end-to-end call latency.
2) Structured outputs: validate JSON schema conformance on 10k prompts (edge cases + long contexts). We'll run automated schema checks and report exact vs near-match failures.
3) Streaming: measure first-byte latency and token throughput at 50/200 rps with streaming enabled; compare perceived UX latency (first 100ms targets) to your current endpoints.

Attached is a short test plan and a sample payload you can use to sanity-check (redwood_feature-parity-test-plan.pdf). Can you share your preferred success thresholds for each test and the sample dataset you want us to use? If you're OK, we'll provision a small dedicated canary (same region) and run the three tests next week.

Next steps / owners:
- ACME: share sample payload & any schema constraints (Alice).
- Redwood: run test plan and share raw logs + summary (Marissa + Rishi).
- If we see regressions vs your baseline, we'll schedule a tuning session (Vivek).

Thanks — aiming to kick off on 4/21 if that works for you.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Subject: Re: ACME feature-parity: post-call recap & next tests

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and aligns with our priorities. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Hyperscaler baseline: for the comparison we use your standard open-model stack vs our current provider (AWS Bedrock + EKS-based routing). Can you include exact request/response traces that show model variant, quantization, and hardware used?
2) For structured outputs, we need strict schema enforcement (we'll provide JSON Schema) and a low false-positive tolerance for near-match.
3) Streaming: our product team cares most about first-byte and first-meaningful-chunk latency; please include perceived latency metrics.

We'll attach a small sample dataset and the JSON Schema — see attached acme_test_payload.json.

We're good to start the canary on 4/21. Can you also provide a HubSpot link to track the test artifacts? I'd like to loop in security later if we need to share any logs.

Appreciate it,
Alice
Product Manager, ACME Corp
alice.chen@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-18T13:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME feature-parity: post-call recap & next tests

Perfect — thanks for the sample. A couple concrete notes on the baseline/tracing and the exact test harness we'll run: 

Baseline & tracing:
- We will tag every request with a test-run id and capture model name, quantization profile, hardware type (A100 vs H100 equivalent), and any kernel/compilation flags. That will be in the raw traces we share.

Test harness (high level):
- Function/tool calling: replay the call graph from your sample payload with 200 concurrent sessions. Measure end-to-end success (tool invoked and results validated), fallback rates, and KV cache hit rates. Success criteria: >= 99% tool-success, median end-to-end latency within 20% of your baseline.
- Structured outputs: run the 10k prompt pass and validate JSON Schema strictness. We'll produce a failure distribution: exact-JSON-failures, near-match (small diffs), and semantic mismatches (e.g., missing fields). Success criteria: exact or acceptable near-match >= 98%.
- Streaming UX: we’ll instrument client-side to capture first-byte and first-meaningful-chunk times. Success criteria: 95th percentile first-byte < 250ms under the 50rps profile.

Differentiators vs hyperscalers we'll highlight in the report:
- More deterministic cold-start behavior through our KV prewarming and continuous batching controls.
- Lower tail latency under mixed workloads due to our smart routing and autoscale policies.
- Transparent quantization profiles and a recommended profile per workload (we'll suggest one for your prompts).

Logistics & owners:
- I'll create a HubSpot record and upload the test artifacts: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ACME-2027-Q2-045
- Rishi: can you provision the canary (dedicated small) in us-west2 and run the harness on 4/21?
- Vivek: please prepare the quantization profile and a short tuning doc we can attach to the results.

If that looks good I'll schedule the run and share the dashboard + raw logs.

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa
